# Commit changes

1. Confirm that the directory is a Git worktree and inspect status and diffs.
2. Preserve unrelated user changes and secrets.
3. Group files by one coherent intent. Stage explicit paths; never use broad staging when unrelated work exists.
4. Run the checks appropriate to each group before committing.
5. Use Conventional Commits with a concise imperative subject and explain the reason in the body only when needed.
6. Show the resulting commit hashes and remaining uncommitted files.

Do not initialize a repository, push, merge, rewrite history, or create a pull request unless separately requested.
